extracted.intended_audience: students, practitioners, and general readers interested in natural philosophy / philosophy of science
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on studying and practicing the physical sciences: principles, methods (observation, analysis, induction), classification, and the formation and verification of theories, with commentary on the intellectual virtues needed. Aimed at preparing readers to conduct systematic examination of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of truth, simplicity, and directness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatsoever is true, simple, and direct is most congenial to human nature; the pursuit and investigation of truth are central human activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preface emphasizes that the love of truth and straightforward presentation are natural and appropriate aims of scientific inquiry ('whatsoever is true, simple, and direct...most congenial to our nature as men'). Work should aim for truth, simplicity, and sincerity in exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from authority; obedience to just and useful principles
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-constituted mind should not submit its faculties to anyone except those who teach by precept or doctrine, or for legitimate, useful reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates intellectual independence: do not accept assertions merely from authority — instead rely on just, lawful, and utility-founded principles when forming beliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Nature and Advantages of Studying Physical Sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding the general nature and benefits of physical science, including how scientific pursuits influence the mind and contribute to well-being and social progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scientific work partly by its contribution to intellectual development and its practical/social advantages (see Part I chapters on influence of science on the mind and society).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Abstract Science as Preparation for Physics
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract science can prepare for the study of physics, but a profound acquaintance with abstract science is not indispensable for clear understanding of physical laws; convictions of truth may be obtained without it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical comprehension of physical laws can be achieved without deep abstract training; know when formal abstraction is necessary and when empirical understanding suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of the Nature and Objects (immediate and collateral) of Physical Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies the immediate and collateral objects of physical science, both in itself and in its application to practical purposes of life, and its influence on societal well-being and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess scientific work by both its intrinsic explanatory power and its practical or societal applications and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience as the Source of our Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience is the primary source of knowledge; includes the dismissal of prejudices and reliance on the evidence of the senses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place empirical observation at the foundation of inquiry; actively reject preconceived prejudices and evaluate sensory evidence critically but principally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of Prejudices
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively dismiss prejudices when forming scientific judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be vigilant for biases and prior presuppositions; ensure they do not distort collection or interpretation of empirical data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of the Senses
rubrics_metrics.description: The senses provide the evidential basis for physical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat sensory reports as the starting point for science, but consider means of verification, repeatability, and instruments that enhance or correct direct sense-perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of Phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic analysis of observed phenomena to identify components, relations, and regularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break down complex phenomena into analyzable parts; use analysis to expose regularities that can be tested and generalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation of Facts and Collection of Instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful observation and comprehensive collection of instances are essential for forming reliable generalizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize accurate, extensive, and well-documented observations; build bodies of instances sufficient to test and confirm proposed laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of Natural Objects and Phenomena, and Nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic classification and consistent nomenclature are necessary for organizing knowledge of natural objects and phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop clear classification schemes and terminology to facilitate comparison, communication, and theory development; avoid ambiguous or inconsistent naming.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Stage of Induction: Discovery of Proximate Causes and Low-General Laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial inductive stage seeks proximate causes and laws of the lowest degree of generality and requires verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin induction by identifying proximate causes and narrowly framed laws; verify these through repeated observation and experiment before attempting broader generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher Degrees of Inductive Generalization; Formation and Verification of Theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher inductive stages involve generalizing to broader laws and forming theories, which must then be verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress from specific verified laws to higher-level generalizations cautiously; construct theories that account for multiple phenomena and design critical tests for their verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision of Physics into Distinct Branches and Their Mutual Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide physical science into coherent branches (forces, constitution of bodies, motion, sound, light, cosmical phenomena, material constituents, imponderable forms) and study their interrelations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize specialized subfields and how they interconnect; evaluate work in context of its branch and its contributions to understanding relations across branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of Material Constituents of the World
rubrics_metrics.description: Study and analyze the material constituents of the world as a core scientific task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate experimental and analytic methods to determine composition and properties of materials; integrate findings into broader physical theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of Imponderable Forms of Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of imponderable (subtle) forms of matter (e.g., heat, electricity, magnetism, as conceived historically) within physical theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate phenomena not easily reduced to particulate matter (in the historical sense) and incorporate reliable observations into coherent explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical Awareness: State of Physical Science Before Major Revolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding the historical state of science prior to the ages of Galileo and Bacon provides perspective on methodological advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use history to judge progress in methods and to avoid past errors; appreciate how methodological changes (e.g., emphasis on experiment) improved reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to Causes of Rapid Scientific Advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze and learn from the causes behind periods of rapid progress in the physical sciences compared with earlier slower advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify institutional, methodological, and technological factors that accelerate discovery to emulate productive conditions for research.
